name: colTabulates
title: Tabulates the values in a matrix by column

origin.description: Tabulates the values in a matrix by row (column).
origin.usage:
colTabulates(x, rows = NULL, cols = NULL, values = NULL, ...,
  useNames = TRUE)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: An integer, logical, or raw NxK matrix.

arguments.name: rows
arguments.text: A vector indicating a subset of rows to operate over. If NULL, no subsetting is done.

arguments.name: cols
arguments.text: A vector indicating a subset of columns to operate over. If NULL, no subsetting is done.

arguments.name: values
arguments.text: A vector of J values to count. If NULL, all unique values are counted.

arguments.name: useNames
arguments.text: If TRUE (default), names attributes of the result are set, otherwise not.

origin.details: The count is an integer. When values is NULL the columns are the sorted observed values, with NA last. An explicit values vector keeps its order. Missing cells are counted in the NA column and are left out of the other columns. A raw matrix has no missing value; a raw subscript that is NA becomes byte 0x00.
origin.value: A K by J integer matrix. K is the number of selected columns and J is the number of values counted.

translation.description: Tabulates the values in a matrix by column.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: An integer matrix, a logical matrix, or a raw matrix stored as uint8. Axis 0 is rows and axis 1 is columns. A logical missing value is None. An integer missing value is None or the R integer NA sentinel. A double matrix is rejected.

arguments.name: rows
arguments.text: 1-based rows to keep, using R's [ rules. None keeps every row. Zero is dropped, negatives exclude, and NA inserts a missing row.

arguments.name: cols
arguments.text: 1-based columns to keep. None keeps every column. The same subscript rules as rows apply.

arguments.name: values
arguments.text: Values to count, in the order of the result columns. None counts each observed value, sorted, with a missing-value column last. An explicit value is coerced to the storage mode of x.

arguments.name: use_names
arguments.text: Accepted for compatibility with useNames. The result is always a plain array; names are not attached.

translation.details: The R function has no .Call, so the counts are computed in NumPy. One result row is one column of x. A missing cell is counted only in the missing-value column. On a raw matrix, NA and out-of-range values coerce to byte 0. The result is int32.
translation.value: An int32 array of shape (selected columns, number of values).
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from matrixstats.rowtabulates import colTabulates

colTabulates(np.tile(np.arange(1, 6), 10).reshape((10, 5), order="F"))
